fields.meta_title: PPC Landing Page: 4 Paid Search Setups | Emergent
fields.meta_description: What a PPC landing page needs after the click: a headline that echoes the keyword, one offer, and four paid search setups built from a prompt.
fields.h1: Build a PPC Landing Page for Every Ad Group
fields.hero_description: Name your ad groups and the offer behind each. Emergent builds the PPC landing page with a headline for every group, and saves each lead with its search term.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds for Paid Clicks
fields.features_subheading: A page that matches the ad in front of it, and the data to judge what each click was worth.
fields.feature_1:
Headlines that follow the keyword

Each visit arrives with a value in the ad's final URL, such as service=water-heater. The page reads that value and swaps in the headline and photo written for the matching ad group.
fields.feature_2:
A page per ad group, by message

Ask for a version of the page per ad group. Emergent copies the layout, rewrites the offer for each group, and gives every version its own address to use as the ad's final URL.
fields.feature_3:
The search term stored on each lead

The search term behind every click reaches the page through the {keyword} parameter in Google Ads. Emergent saves it on the lead's row, beside the campaign name and the visit time.
fields.feature_4:
One way forward from the page

Nothing on the page needs to link away from the offer. Ask Emergent to drop the site menu and footer links, and the form or call button becomes the visitor's only next step.
fields.feature_5:
Split tests started with a sentence

Two headlines can run behind one ad at once. Send Emergent a message asking for a variant, and it divides visitors evenly between the versions and records which one each lead saw.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can move to any host

Every file behind the page exports to your GitHub repository, lead database included. Publish on Emergent under your own domain, or host the code on servers your team runs.

fields.usecase_heading: Four PPC Pages by Campaign Type
fields.tab_content_1:
The headline repeats what the searcher typed

Northgate Plumbing bids on four services in Denver and runs one page behind all four ad groups. Each ad's final URL carries a service value. A water heater search opens on "Water heater repair, same day" instead of a general plumbing headline, and the lead is saved with its ad group.
fields.tab_content_2:
After 6 PM, the call button becomes a callback form

Patients searching on a phone for an emergency dentist tap a Larkspur Dental call ad and land on a page with one large call button. Until 6 PM it rings the front desk. After that the button turns into a callback request, and at 8 AM the front desk gets the list of patients waiting for a call.
fields.tab_content_3:
A waitlist where the checkout used to be

Halden Outdoor's Shopping ad sends clicks to a product page for the Ridgeline 2 tent, priced at the same $249 the ad shows. When the tent sells out, the page replaces the checkout button with a waitlist form. Ad manager Jonas Berg gets a Slack direct message asking whether to pause the ad.
fields.tab_content_4:
Ledgerline tests two headlines on the same ad

Visitors from Ledgerline's paid search ads are split evenly between two headlines: "Invoices that chase themselves" and "Stop writing payment reminders". After 1,000 visits each, the second headline has brought in 61 free trials against 38 for the first. Moving all traffic to the winner is a message to Emergent.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a PPC Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Every paid click is bought before the visitor reads a word. The page has one job: keep the promise the ad has made.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Give each ad group its own page
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Put the search in the headline
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Keep the price the ad quoted
fields.howto_step_1_des: Group keywords by what the searcher wants, then give each group a page. Someone typing drain cleaning and someone typing water heater repair need different headlines and offers, even when the same plumber answers both calls.
fields.howto_step_2_des: The first line a visitor reads should repeat the words they searched, or come close. Google Ads rates landing page experience on how relevant the page is to the search and the ad, and that rating is one part of Quality Score.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Drop the site menu and any second offer. A paid visitor who wanders off to read the company history has cost a click without converting. Keep one form or one call button, and repeat it further down on long pages.
fields.howto_step_4_des: When the ad says $249 or free shipping, the page says the same thing above the fold. A mismatch reads as bait to the visitor. A product that sells out should change the page before more paid clicks arrive.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Pass the keyword in the final URL
fields.howto_step_5_des: Add the {keyword} ValueTrack parameter to the final URL suffix, along with a campaign value. Google fills in the keyword that triggered the ad, and the page can store it with the lead or use it to choose the headline.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test the page on every device
fields.howto_step_6_des: Open the page on a phone and on a desktop browser before launch, press every button and submit the form once. Then confirm the ad's final URL opens the page itself, not a redirect to the home page or an error.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Track the form submit or the call as a conversion, then compare each ad group's cost per conversion. A page with cheap clicks and no conversions is the expensive one. Rewrite the headline before you raise the bid.

claims_to_source: With cost-per-click bidding in Google Ads, the advertiser pays only when someone clicks the ad, and an auction based on Ad Rank decides placement and price
Landing page experience is one of the components of Quality Score in Google Ads, judged on relevance and on whether the page gives people what the ad led them to expect
The ValueTrack parameter {keyword} inserts the keyword that triggered the ad into the final URL or a final URL suffix
